T1003.002.attack_name: OS Credential Dumping: Security Account Manager (SAM)

d3fend_countermeasures.name: Restrict Access to SAM Registry Hive
Windows Defender Credential Guard
d3fend_countermeasures.verification_script:
# Check if Credential Guard is active via WMI
$Guard = Get-CimInstance -Namespace "Root\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard" -ClassName "MSFT_DeviceGuard" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($Guard -and $Guard.SecurityServicesRunning -contains 1) {
    Write-Output "Compliant: Credential Guard is active."
    exit 0
}
Write-Output "Non-Compliant: Credential Guard is not active."
exit 1

d3fend_countermeasures.name: Linux /proc Process Memory Restrictions
d3fend_countermeasures.verification_script:
# Check if hidepid option is set for proc mount
if grep -q "hidepid=" /proc/mounts; then
    echo "Compliant: proc filesystem hidepid parameter is active"
    exit 0
fi
echo "Non-Compliant: hidepid option is not set for proc mount"
exit 1

d3fend_countermeasures.name: Shadow File Permissions Isolation
d3fend_countermeasures.verification_script:
# Verify permission on /etc/shadow is 600 or 000
perms=$(stat -c "%a" /etc/shadow 2>/dev/null)
if [ "$perms" = "600" ] || [ "$perms" = "000" ]; then
    echo "Compliant: shadow file permissions are restricted ($perms)"
    exit 0
fi
echo "Non-Compliant: shadow file permissions are exposed ($perms)"
exit 1
